title: Chinese ink painting
examples: What materials do you need for Chinese ink painting?
Can ink painting be used for portraits?
How is calligraphy different from painting?

explain.say: Today we learn about Chinese ink painting techniques. It uses simple tools to make art.
The brush and ink are central to this art form. The ink is often made from soot and glue.
Chinese landscapes are a major subject. They often show mountains and rivers together. This is called shan shui.
Calligraphy is the art of beautiful writing. In this art, the characters are as important as the pictures.
In daily life, you see this idea in modern logo design. Many brands use simple, flowing lines like ink.

items: Black and white contrast is strong

explain.say: A common mistake is pressing too hard with the brush. This makes the lines look thick and clumsy.

faq.q: What is the difference between calligraphy and painting?
faq.a: Calligraphy focuses on the beauty of the written characters themselves. Painting uses the brush to create images, like scenery.
asks: Do I write or draw in ink painting?

faq.q: What does 'shan shui' mean in art?
faq.a: Shan shui translates to 'mountain and water' in Chinese. It describes the grand, harmonious pairing of these natural elements in art.
asks: What is the meaning of mountain water?
Where does the term shan shui come from?

faq.q: Can I use color in Chinese ink painting?
faq.a: Traditional ink painting emphasizes the tonal range of black ink. While color can be added, the focus remains on ink wash.
asks: Is it always black and white?

faq.q: What kind of brush should I use?
faq.a: You need a brush with fine, absorbent bristles. The quality of the brush greatly affects the line's flow.
asks: What kind of bristles work best?
Do I need a special brush?

faq.q: Is this art style only from China?
faq.a: While originating in China, the principles of ink wash have influenced art in many East Asian cultures.
asks: Are there other countries that use this?

facts: Ink painting often uses mineral and plant pigments mixed with soot.
Shan shui compositions aim to capture the vastness of nature.
Calligraphy requires mastery over brush control and pressure.
The art form values negative space as much as the painted subject.

quiz.say: The harmonious pairing of mountains and water in Chinese art is called:
quiz.why: This specific term describes the core subject matter of the landscape.

wrong.0: Calligraphy is the art of writing characters, not landscapes.
wrong.1: Brushwork describes the skill used, not the subject matter.
wrong.3: Ink wash describes the technique, not the subject matter itself.

quiz.say: When practicing calligraphy, the focus is primarily on:
quiz.why: Calligraphy is fundamentally about the aesthetic execution of written script.

wrong.0: Traditional calligraphy emphasizes monochrome ink tones.
wrong.1: The paper size is a constraint, not the primary focus of mastery.
wrong.3: Speed is secondary; controlled form is more important.

quiz.say: In ink painting, the empty space around the subject is considered:
quiz.why: The empty space helps the viewer focus on the painted elements.

wrong.0: It has artistic value beyond just being a background.
wrong.1: It is a crucial element that balances the composition.
wrong.3: Filling all space removes the sense of vastness.
